posts.angle: Teach the complete reset instead of a loose accessory bundle
posts.headline: The vinyl-care gift is a three-step loop
posts.copy: Clean only a supported record. Let it dry completely. Inspect a correctly sized fresh inner before rehousing. The sleeve earns its place after the clean—not as another unopened supply beside the turntable.
posts.assetBrief: Original vertical three-step flow using a generic record edge, drying clock, and open inner sleeve; no album art, logos, or product photography.
posts.altText: Three-step diagram showing a vinyl record cleaned, dried completely, and placed into a fresh inner sleeve.

posts.angle: Put record material identification before cleaning
posts.headline: Before wet cleaning a record, identify the medium
posts.copy: Modern vinyl is not shellac, lacquer, a picture disc, or an unknown specialty material. Check exact instructions, label stability, record size, and a clean work surface. Uncertain medium means stop—not experiment.
posts.assetBrief: Six original slides with generic disc silhouettes, material question marks, label warning, edge handling, instruction manual, and stop card.
posts.altText: Carousel reminding collectors to identify record material, label condition, size, and instructions before wet cleaning.

posts.angle: Choose a cleaner by real queue size and maintenance tolerance
posts.headline: Batch bath or one-record pad? Count the queue first
posts.copy: Choose a manual bath for a named compatible batch with water, drying, and cleanup space. Choose a pad-and-mist ritual for one compatible arrival at a time. Skip both when the collector wants professional or powered cleaning.
posts.assetBrief: Original branching flowchart from one record versus small batch to compact pad versus basin, ending in space and maintenance checks.
posts.altText: Decision flow comparing a batch record-cleaning bath with a one-record pad workflow.

posts.angle: Choose sleeve support and thickness by the real jacket
posts.headline: The best inner sleeve still has to fit the jacket
posts.copy: Confirm 12 versus 7 inches, inspect for debris or creases, test the tightest representative jacket, and compare supported versus thin HDPE handling. Never transfer a full batch from the package alone.
posts.assetBrief: Five original slides with size ruler, inspection light, tight jacket, supported sleeve, thin sleeve, and sample-first rule.
posts.altText: Carousel showing record size, sleeve inspection, jacket clearance, and supported-versus-thin inner-sleeve checks.

posts.angle: Protect record history while changing the contact sleeve
posts.headline: New inner sleeve does not mean throw away the old art
posts.copy: Hook: stop before the printed inner hits the trash. Show a generic lyric sleeve kept beside a newly sleeved record, with edge handling and a fully dry check. End: replace the contact surface, preserve the information.
posts.assetBrief: Original unbranded storyboard with generic printed insert, clean sleeve, dry-check icon, and side-by-side storage; no album artwork.
posts.altText: Short video storyboard retaining a printed original inner while a fully dry record moves into a fresh sleeve.

posts.angle: Make the partial and no-purchase branches explicit
posts.headline: When the vinyl-care pair should be one item—or none
posts.copy: Buy only the cleaner when fresh fitted sleeves already exist. Buy only sleeves when a trusted wet-clean routine exists. Pair them for a named compatible queue. Skip both for uncertain media, no work area, or a preferred professional service.
posts.assetBrief: Original three-column Pair, One item, and Skip card with generic basin, pad, sleeve, work-surface, and stop icons.
posts.altText: Decision card showing when to pair a record cleaner and inner sleeves, buy one item, or skip both.
